decision: Keep CALABARZON visibly in progress. This checkpoint records the current source-backed leads and specific gaps; it is not a complete fish checklist, a completed region, or a public species release.

historicalSourcesWithSomeSpeciesLevelRes.note: Four historical locality assertions from four CC0 museum specimens; shared coordinate is withheld; the NFRDI reports are separate landed-catch or source leads.

Separately, all 17 dated CAS source records with CC0 rights and supported name crosswalks are admitted only to the internal historical research ledger. One MZUSP source item remains held for rank, locality and reuse conflicts. No public rows or points were added.
Twelve dated-paper table assertions in a separate reviewed projection; three source-family conflicts remain held; not a whole-river or current-presence list.

Four historical literature-checklist assertions and three historical CAS preserved-specimen locality assertions are prepared. The CAS rows retain CONTINENT_INVALID flags and have no map points; three checklist candidates remain held. The National Museum zero-result search is bounded, and two FishBase crosswalk candidates remain held pending primary catalog and reuse review.

Three CC0 CAS preserved specimens dated 1941-10-18 have exact Santa Cruz River waterBody and locality text. They are research-ledger historical assertions only; broad georeference uncertainty prevents map points, and current presence is not inferred.

A JICA-hosted 2017 EIA provides a four-station 2016 estuarine fishery matrix; only Station 4 is assigned to the Maalimango River mouth. Five species-rank names match the GBIF Backbone while three fish rows remain genus-level/alternative. Mixed observation/interview basis, no vouchers and unverified reuse keep all evidence research-only; no current presence, geometry or public assertion is inferred.

The 2018 primary study directly reports source-named fish taxon labels at stations SW-YY-1/2/3. Field dates, per-taxon counts, vouchers and station coordinates are not given in the reviewed text. Automated COL XR matches are crosswalk proposals only; no species assertion or public row was added.

materialHeldOrUnavailable: Tayabas River: official abstract describes 15 aggregate species, but its table is unavailable and item-specific reuse rights are unresolved; three exact river-locality GBIF fish searches returned zero. A separate CC0 Naturalis fish specimen has locality Tayabas only, with no date, coordinate, or waterbody, so it remains unassigned.
Seven San Pablo lakes: one historical aggregate study lead; per-lake species rows held pending item-specific rights.
Manila Bay: historic trawl table and seven additional CAS named-bay candidates remain held; broad named-bay geometry is not a legal or Cavite boundary.
Brackish and estuarine leads: no admitted assertions tied to reviewed station salinity.
Several rivers, lakes, bays, wetlands, reservoirs and streams remain unreviewed or have only bounded locality-string checks.
Dagatan Lake: a DENR plan lists five local fish names, but no scientific identities, specimens or fish sampling date; item-level reuse terms and current protection status are unresolved.

The 11 new BMB/DENR CALABARZON water/habitat leads had 32 exact-name GBIF Actinopterygii searches across waterBody/locality fields (including five candidate spelling variants); all returned zero. This is a bounded discovery gap, not evidence of fish absence.

SEAFDEC 2016 Table 2 identifies a Bal-on Reservoir site and NIFEP group activities for several CALABARZON waters, but the San Pablo/Tadlak grouping is not allocated to individual lakes and six Rizal river sanctuaries are unnamed. The table gives no contemporary species survey.

Bal-on Reservoir: the bounded 2026-10-26 indexed-web search found only the SEAFDEC NIFEP site mention, without a municipality, fish taxa or geometry. It did not locate an independent locality record or dated survey; that retrieval gap is not fish-absence evidence.

SEAFDEC's 2016 proceedings reports a 7 ha Dagatan Lake in San Antonio at coordinates rounded to whole minutes. Figure 4 labels six fishes (five binomials and Oreochromis sp.); five received automated COL XR match proposals, including Trichogaster pectoralis as a synonym of Trichopodus pectoralis. No sampling details, locality crosswalk or reuse permission is provided, so labels remain research-only and are not assigned to either Dagatan/Pagatan scope lead.
Taal Lake: four exact National Museum GBIF text-field queries for Taal and Amphilophus citrinellus returned zero; this version- and field-bounded discovery result is not evidence of fish absence.

Taal Lake: two coordinate-envelope National Museum specimens match FishBase Taal catalog entries by catalog number, taxon and year, but GBIF lacks locality/waterBody and FishBase is CC BY-NC 4.0; primary catalog verification and reuse remain pending.
Taal Lake: the FishBase FW code for one GBIF/SEAFDEC catalog match conflicts with SEAOBIS institution/collection codes; verify provenance before using either candidate.

Laguna de Bay museum batch: the official CAS IPT archive directly matched all 17 collection-qualified source items, and all 17 are admitted only as historical research-ledger evidence. One MZUSP item remains held because the portal interprets it at family rank, conflicts on locality assertion and license, and gives no waterBody value. No absence or current-presence claim is inferred.

Bacoor Bay and Cañacao Bay: six bounded GBIF all-taxon waterBody/locality text searches returned five unique same-dataset records (four Mollusca, one taxon-unmatched); zero fish-identified candidates. Text labels conflict with some waterBody values, so no bay-specific fish assertion, absence inference, geometry or salinity conclusion is made.

Cavite Ecological Profile 2024: Table 4.25 reports 11 province-wide municipal-fisheries common-name labels and season/peak/lean periods, credited to the Office of the Provincial Agriculturist. It provides no scientific names or row-level waterbody attribution; retain as a research lead only, with reuse terms unverified.

Manila Bay: the official NFRDI 2020 annual-report summary reports 225 species types in aggregate landed catch across eight landing sites and identifies Sardinella fimbriata at 19%. The summary does not provide a site-specific species table, Rosario attribution or capture positions; no occurrence assertion is inferred.

Manila Bay: the National Museum v1.38 CC BY 4.0 fish archive and GBIF index match seven dated sourceStateProvince=Cavite specimens, but all seven lack locality and waterBody fields. The archive describes landing-site, market, port and nearby-sea contexts without per-record capture-origin rules; no species-waterbody assertions or map points are added.

Tayabas Bay: six historical CAS fish specimen candidates have explicit GBIF waterBody text but remain held because GBIF CC0 metadata conflicts with CAS collection database no-redistribution terms. Two BFAR/NFRDI/NSAP poster leads cover 2015-2022 and 2018-2022, but their item records show no reuse license; no species assertions are admitted.

Iyam-Alitaaw (Iyam) River: a 2015 primary paper reports six species-rank taxa and two genus-only records from wet-season sampling in 2010 and 2011. All six binomials exactly match the pinned CoL XR index, but the Zenodo CC BY 4.0 declaration conflicts with current NUS publisher terms; no public species rows are admitted. Eight corrected GBIF text searches returned zero, which is not evidence of absence.
Cambantoc River: four bounded corrected CoL XR Actinopterygii text-field searches for Cambantoc and Cambantoc River across waterBody and locality returned zero; this is not evidence of fish absence.

Morong River: one historical GBIF/CAS specimen candidate is held without a species row or coordinates. Its georeferenced geography conflicts with the CALABARZON/Rizal lead, same-name river identity is unresolved, and CAS redistribution terms conflict with GBIF CC0 metadata.

Tres Cruzes: BMB/Cavite/NIA sources support a managed water-storage research lead, but exact impoundment identity and extent are unverified. The 15.65 ha inventory area and 911.1 ha dam-table area-covered figure are not adopted; exact GBIF name screens returned zero, not fish-absence evidence.
Noveleta Mangrove Area: official site and area statements reviewed, but their scopes do not define a water boundary; no fish list or site-level fish evidence is available in the page.

Official EMB Island C EIS: direct PDF review confirms a 17-row Table 2.2-46 (15 fish-labeled and two invertebrate rows) for fishing grounds of Rosario, Noveleta, and Cavite City near a proposed reclamation. Linked only to broad Manila Bay context; row-level localities and reuse terms remain open, no names were transcribed, and no species occurrence is inferred.

Maalimango River mouth: historical 2016 Station 4 fishery matrix is supported, but whole-channel geometry, seasonal/current status, independent field identification and item-specific reuse rights remain unresolved; stations 1?3 are unassigned.
evidenceReadout.zeroResultMeaning: Exact-locality zeroes are limited to searched spellings, fields and filters; they are bounded discovery gaps, not fish-absence findings. Alternate spellings may reveal records, as with Santa Cruz River. Waterbird monitoring and historical common-name lists are not species-level fish presence evidence.

historicalGenusLevelResearchEvidence.note: A 2024 primary study reports 48 juvenile Tilapia sp. sampled at upstream, midstream, and downstream Maragondon River stations in April 2023. The authors withheld species resolution due to possible hybridization and gene-pool uncertainty; this is genus-level historical evidence only. It does not establish current presence, catchability, full-river coverage, salinity, or geometry.

historicalAggregateFisheryEvidence.note: An official DA-NFRDI 2020 report summarizes 1,197 metric tons of landed catch across eight Manila Bay sites and reports 225 species types, with Sardinella fimbriata at 19%. It does not allocate the taxon or share to Rosario or a capture site; no species assertion is admitted.

historicalSpeciesLevelClaimsHeld.note: A 2018 Maragondon River sampling study published in 2019 names Oreochromis niloticus. Specimen identification and item-specific reuse remain unverified. The cited DLSU-D thesis was not obtained; the current official library FAQ reports A.I.R. temporarily suspended and requires author permission for full text. The later 2024 study reports Tilapia sp. and withholds species resolution. No species assertion or public projection is admitted.

Martinez (2018) directly reports seven distinct fish taxon labels across three Ylang-Yang River stations, but not the collection date, per-taxon counts, vouchers or station coordinates. Three labels receive exact accepted species matches from pinned COL XR; one exact synonym mapping, two source-spelling variants and one genus-only label remain unresolved. Research-only source review; no assertion was imported, no current presence or complete river list is inferred, and the separate slash-form Ylang ylang/Rio Grande record remains unresolved.

The official AIIB EIA names Oreochromis niloticus and Mugil cephalus as subsistence-fished in the Labac River section; both receive exact accepted species-name matches under the explicit CoL XR checklist key. The crosswalk does not verify field identification, catch date, reach, method or vouchers. No species assertion or current-presence claim is added.

openGaps.reason: Ninety-six selected named water/habitat leads are seeded across CALABARZON water types. The official 2024 Cavite profile adds source-reported route context for six major rivers and three separate Cavite channel leads; this does not establish a complete waterbody denominator. Historical inventories and river profiles remain partial and differently classified. GBIF zeroes remain bounded discovery only; no absence or current fish status is inferred. For Labac River, the two EIA names now have exact CoL XR accepted-name matches, but field identification, date, station, method and vouchers remain unverified.
openGaps.nextAction: Continue source-derived locality and feature-identity review across all CALABARZON water types; resolve the DENR 2021 aggregate counts and obtain a named, auditable inventory before claiming complete regional coverage.

openGaps.reason: The official CAS IPT archive verifies 17 exact collection-qualified Laguna de Bay source items; all 17 have supported source-name crosswalks and are admitted only as historical source-locality evidence in the research ledger. One unique MZUSP source item is matched by collection, catalog number and occurrence ID. Its two source-linked copies disagree on rank metadata: one says Espécie and one omits rank, while both portal interpretations resolve to family Ariidae. Its Laguna de Bay locality text is present, but the portal reports no geospatial location and the record has no waterBody field. The source reports CC BY-NC while GBIF reports CC BY, so the item remains held from public app projections pending provider-specific reuse clarification. This batch does not establish current presence or a complete lake checklist.
openGaps.nextAction: Obtain authoritative source-level clarification from MZUSP on provider-level reuse terms before public use; preserve source rank differences and the Laguna de Bay locality string as text-only evidence with no point or waterbody assignment.

openGaps.reason: Fourteen corrected GBIF candidates group into ten museum catalog identities. Direct Field Museum and CAS archives confirm two FMNH and six CAS SU(ICH) records with Balayan Bay locality text; the eight are admitted only as dated historical research-ledger evidence, with source date precision and all GBIF flags preserved. The CAS archive publishes its selected rows under CC0, and source catalog 28340 plus GBIF spelling variants resolve nomenclaturally to Planiliza macrolepis. A direct UMMZ Fish archive release 1.115 check confirms catalog 100346, Sillago sihama and Balayan Bay locality under CC BY 4.0, but the event date is blank; it remains an undated research-only locality candidate. Five GBIF citations resolve to one dated NMNH USNM 122919 item; dataset and row reuse are CC0. The direct NMNH record gives D 5115 OR D 5116; a 1910 station table places both in a Balayan Bay/Verde Island Passage area, while a 2015 specimen paper reports 623 m off northeastern Mindoro, consistent with D 5115 but not naming it. Keep the one item held from a Balayan Bay-only assertion because exact station and exclusive waterbody scope remain unresolved. Eight candidates have dated historical locality evidence, one undated locality candidate, and five duplicate citation rows remain held as one item. No current-presence or complete-checklist claim is made.
openGaps.nextAction: Rights are no longer the blocker for USNM 122919: CC0 is verified at the NMNH dataset and GBIF-row levels. Keep the five citations grouped as one item and held from a Balayan Bay-only assertion until station D 5115 versus D 5116 and the conflicting broad locality wording are reconciled; if a combined Balayan Bay/Verde Island Passage area is modeled, preserve it as a distinct combined scope. Keep coordinates, map points and current-presence claims out of the app.

openGaps.reason: Official sources identify Gapan River in Ternate and a one-kilometer Adopt-a-Waterbody segment; PRA supplies the Gapan (Sapang) name variant. Six bounded GBIF exact-name field searches returned zero, and no dated official fish survey surfaced in bounded public searches. Neither result proves fish absence or defines the full channel. A GeoNames point was found, but its 1.57-km separation from the nearest modelled stream segment leaves the channel crosswalk inconclusive.
openGaps.nextAction: Ask NAMRIA through an authorized public-products inquiry whether it can identify a permitted Gapan channel dataset or suitable map; ask DENR, PRA and Ternate LGU for the one-kilometer program segment endpoints or a station-to-channel crosswalk. MarIS is restricted to the Hydrography Branch intranet and was not accessed. Continue dated fish and water-quality searches for the exact reach; keep the full-channel geometry, salinity and species unresolved until source-backed.

openGaps.nextAction: Seek current official protected-area/LGU hydrography and dated freshwater fish surveys for each source-named reach. Preserve Mamba/Cacabay as one unresolved compound name and do not assign either full channel to one province.

openGaps.reason: EMB sources identify two nearby Tagbac program station groups; the 2013 DEM-derived network has adjacent connected lines near those stations, but this modelled continuity does not confirm a single named watercourse or full-channel geometry.

openGaps.reason: The provincial profile supplies source-named course and reported-length context for Bacoor, Cavite San Juan and Labac but no station coordinates or channel geometry. The 2023 AIIB EIA reports subsistence fishing of Oreochromis niloticus and Mugil cephalus without a fish date, station, reach, method or voucher; reuse terms are unverified. The 2017 JICA Volume 1 summary reports eight fish and three crustacean species but does not name the watercourse or station and does not tie those taxa to San Juan River. A separate JICA-hosted EIA supplies an eight-row fishery matrix at four 2016 estuarine stations, including the Maalimango River mouth; the matching counts suggest a relationship, but no explicit cross-reference was found, so the summary stays unassigned to San Juan. No current presence or reusable channel geometry is established for the three target rivers. A third-party CvSU accreditation-material mirror lists the 2014 Labac fish-study title but not its data; an official CvSU page lists a separate 2018-2020 macroinvertebrate/water-quality project. An official-hosted 2015 Labac-Alemang watershed assessment is discoverable by abstract, but the PDF returned 403 and no fish taxa were confirmed. An apparent 16-station fish passage came from a Scribd document with inconsistent and unrelated contents, and is excluded as a false positive.
openGaps.nextAction: Keep the Volume 1 aggregate unassigned to San Juan. Request authorized copies and item-specific reuse terms for the 2014 CvSU Labac fish study and the 2015 Labac-Alemang watershed assessment; verify any fish dates, stations, methods, vouchers and identifications before use. Exclude the unrelated Scribd thesis passage unless its primary provenance is independently established. Seek dated, station-resolved fish evidence and permitted channel geometry for Bacoor, Cavite San Juan and Labac, plus a permitted Maalimango channel trace. Preserve the 2016 San Juan mouth salinity as point-specific historical evidence only; Volume 3 was not located.

openGaps.reason: Bacoor City's official Ecological Profile names five additional river and creek research leads and describes general household inland fishing, but it supplies no taxa, catch dates, watercourse-specific stations, or permitted channel geometry. Some watercourses cross into neighboring cities. A 2014 South Septage Treatment Plant EIS describes Zapote-Bacoor connectivity and contains undated observation/interview statements about fish, but no taxa, dated fish sampling, reproducible method, coordinates or vouchers; it does not establish fish presence or absence. A bounded GBIF Actinopterygii text screen of six named rivers/creeks and their short names/alias across waterBody and locality fields returned zero indexed text matches (26/26 successful); this is not evidence of fish absence. The DLSU Animo Repository catalog lists a 1984 print thesis on fish and other materials at three Manila Bay river mouths, including Zapote, but the thesis is unavailable online and the catalog supplies no taxa or survey details.
openGaps.nextAction: If the project owner chooses, send the prepared access inquiry to DLSU Libraries for accession TU03120. Confirm external consultation or an authorized scan, item-specific reuse terms, sampling dates, stations, methods and fish names before any assertion. Continue independent station-resolved fish and permitted channel-geometry research for the remaining Bacoor inland waters.

openGaps.reason: The official CvSU Research Journal July–December 2022 issue contains a selected-site shrimp survey with six source-named taxa and site-aggregated counts at four Cañas watershed locations; it is not fish evidence, a complete waterbody inventory, or evidence of absence at sites where the study counted zero. Its introduction says seven crustaceans once while its abstract, results, conclusion and table support six. The same paper cites a separate 2017 CvSU fish-and-crustacean bachelor thesis, but the thesis and fish table have not been retrieved. A separate 2016 CvSU thesis abstract reports SRTM/ArcMap watershed delineation and GPS field validation of boundaries and river networks, but no GIS layer, coordinates or positional-accuracy results were retrieved; the watershed boundary remains not delineated here. The provincial profile still provides no channel geometry; source-site coordinates in the shrimp paper were not visually reviewed, and item-specific reuse terms remain unresolved. The bounded exact-name GBIF fish screen returned zero, which does not indicate fish absence.
openGaps.nextAction: Use the official CvSU E-Library title/author search and, after confirming eligibility, the library Thesis Abstract Delivery Program to request the cited 2017 CvSU thesis on fish and crustaceans. Separately request the 2016 watershed thesis GIS deliverables and item-specific data-use terms. Visually inspect the 2022 sampling-site figure only if exact site-coordinate work is needed; independently crosswalk named sites to channels, tributaries and permitted geometry. Keep shrimp rows research-only, do not infer a whole-river or fish checklist, and keep boundary status not-delineated until source geometry is inspected and validated.
